entries.providerBehavior: A Jira label update replaces the whole label set; it never appends to the previous set.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: WorkItem.labels equals the full native label set of each read: the after-read carries the replacement set and never the accumulated union.

entries.providerBehavior: Jira custom fields carry tenant-specific ids with inconsistent native typing (numeric values arrive as strings, select values arrive as objects).
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Every declared mapping feeds its normalized label destination as typed data (numeric string parsed to a number before rendering, select object reduced to its value); unmapped custom fields are visibly unrepresented and no raw customfield_* key crosses the boundary.

entries.providerBehavior: Jira workflow transitions are provider data; executing them is a separate write operation.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Every native status in the WorkflowMap carries a closed delivery alias and a named transition mechanism; the read path executes no transition.

entries.providerBehavior: Jira may omit the comment payload entirely (permission or paging causes) instead of returning an empty comment list.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: WorkItem.comments is absent when the payload was omitted (comment set unknown) and a present empty array only when the provider asserted an empty set; omission never collapses into [].

entries.providerBehavior: Jira may omit the native updated timestamp on some issue shapes.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: WorkItem.updatedAt is absent when the provider omits updated (activity unknown) and is never derived from comments, ordering, or a clock; a fresh/stale classification is not fabricated for absence.

entries.providerBehavior: The done transition is resolved from the declared workflow map; a POST transitions call with the mapped native status is the write.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: transition-work-item posts the map-declared done native status and succeeds only on a 2xx response.

entries.providerBehavior: Jira labels are replaced as a full array, so a named lifecycle sweep must preserve unnamed labels.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: write-work-item computes the target set from provider-asserted labels, removes only named labels, adds delivered, and preserves vendor labels.
